explanation: Parametrize the shown left half by r(t) = (4cos(t), sin(t)), π/2 ≤ t ≤ 3π/2. Then 4y/x = tan(t) and ds = √(16sin²(t)+cos²(t)) dt = √(15sin²(t)+1) dt, giving d. The integrand is singular at both endpoints, so this is an improper integral that does not converge to a finite value; d correctly expresses it.
